title: Worktrees work, but not on this repo yet

text:
## The watcher was blinded by my own reload hold

I guessed the watcher had no error check. **It already had one** — `pageerror`, console errors, and a blank-page check, all there before today.

The real bug is `is_held()`: while a reload hold is active it defers every check **with no ceiling**. My break at 11:14 happened entirely inside my own 3-minute hold, so the watcher never looked — not while it was broken, not while it was fixed.

The hold I take to protect you from seeing half-written files is exactly what stopped anything from noticing the site was down. It is now capped at 60 seconds.

**A second bug fell out of it:** `health-supervisor.mjs` watched `health.mjs` with a single-path `fs.watch`, which Windows silently orphans on an atomic write. That is why `restarts` has sat at 0 and why the watcher is still running old rules. Now watches the directory.

## Worktrees work — I ran them

The minion wrote both scripts but **could not execute a single command** — its shell refused every `node` and every `git worktree`. So I ran them at harvest, and the first run failed instantly: `Cannot find package 'express'`. A worktree checks out tracked files only, and `node_modules` is gitignored. Fixed by junctioning it from the main checkout. Second run: worktree up, server on a free port, page served.

```
node Server/worktree-up.mjs <name>     # tree + server + url
node Server/worktree-down.mjs <name>   # stop and clean up
```

## But it cannot do the job you want yet — and this is the important part

A worktree contains **only committed files**. This repo has **359 modified and 115 untracked paths**, including the entire `public/framework/ai/v/` directory.

The test worktree had **no V3 in it at all.** Its AI page was the pre-today version.

So the isolation you asked for is built and works, and every page worth testing in isolation is invisible to it until the work is committed. That moves "how does this repo get committed" from housekeeping to **the blocker for the whole idea.**

## What needs you

1. **Commit, or grant me a branch.** Without it there is no worktree testing, and `stash@{0}` still holds the only copy of some work.
2. **Restart the health supervisor** — the fixes are on disk but the running process (pid 34636) is on old rules, and the bug above is precisely why it never picked them up.
3. **A Bash permission rule** — a CLI minion can write files but cannot run anything, so it can build and never prove. I have to run every proof myself at harvest.
